title: Like-Kind Exchange — Recognized Gain and Substituted Basis (§1031, 2026 baseline)
scenario: Dalton exchanges a warehouse used in a trade or business (real property) with an adjusted basis of $300,000 and a fair market value of $500,000. In the exchange Dalton receives replacement real property worth $460,000 plus $40,000 of cash boot. The transaction qualifies as a §1031 like-kind exchange of real property held for business use. On the 2026 law baseline (§1031 applies to real property only), round to the nearest dollar.

tasks.prompt: Requirement 1 — Compute Dalton's realized gain on the exchange.
tasks.explanation: Realized gain = amount realized − adjusted basis. Amount realized = replacement property $460,000 + cash boot $40,000 = $500,000. Realized gain = $500,000 − $300,000 = $200,000.

tasks.prompt: Requirement 2 — Compute the gain Dalton must recognize.
tasks.explanation: In a §1031 exchange, recognized gain = the LESSER of realized gain ($200,000) or boot received ($40,000) = $40,000. Boot triggers gain recognition up to its amount.

tasks.prompt: Requirement 3 — Compute Dalton's basis in the replacement real property.
tasks.explanation: Substituted basis = basis of property given up ($300,000) − boot received ($40,000) + gain recognized ($40,000) = $300,000. The deferred gain is preserved in the replacement property's basis.

tasks.prompt: Requirement 4 — Compute the gain deferred through the exchange.
tasks.explanation: Deferred gain = realized gain $200,000 − recognized gain $40,000 = $160,000. This deferral is what the lower replacement basis will recapture on a future taxable disposition.
